page: Amazon Web Services c8i.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2211.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 34.45 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is highly competitive, reaching 2952.0 on Geekbench, which ranks in the top 10%. For machine learning workloads, the processor's Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) support enables efficient small-model LLM inference, achieving a top-tier text generation speed of 348.03 tokens/sec on a 135M parameter model. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks generally align with the middle 50% of tested systems.

Given its compute-focused resource density, the c8i.4xlarge offers a balanced cost-to-performance profile for CPU-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The high-speed DDR5 memory and dedicated Intel Xeon cores make it highly suitable for batch processing, software compilation, text processing, and web serving. It is also well-suited for running small-scale machine learning inference tasks that leverage CPU-based matrix acceleration.

This hardware profile is optimized for compute-heavy workloads, including software compilation, text processing, web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
